module_title: Amendment of Pleadings, Registration, and Power of Attorney
introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams and corporate litigators, this level explores the strict limitations on altering your pleadings mid-trial, the devastating consequences of failing to register a conveyancing deed, and the mechanics of the Power of Attorney.

core_concepts.title: Amendment of Pleadings (Order VI, Rule 17)
core_concepts.description:
Courts allow parties to amend their plaint or written statement to determine the real questions in controversy, but there is a massive catch.
- The Proviso (The Restriction): No application for amendment shall be allowed **after the trial has commenced**, unless the court comes to the conclusion that in spite of 'due diligence', the party could not have raised the matter before the commencement of trial.
- General Rule: An amendment that changes the entire fundamental nature/character of the suit, or takes away a legal right accrued to the other side by the lapse of time (limitation), will NOT be allowed.

core_concepts.title: Conveyancing: The Mandate of Registration
core_concepts.description:
A beautifully drafted Sale Deed is worthless if it violates the Registration Act, 1908.
- Section 17 of Registration Act: Compulsory Registration is required for any non-testamentary instrument (like a Sale or Gift deed) which purports to create or extinguish any interest in **immovable property of the value of ₹100 or upwards**, and leases of immovable property from year to year or exceeding one year.
- Section 49 Consequence: If a document required to be registered is NOT registered, it shall NOT affect any immovable property comprised therein, nor be received as evidence of any transaction affecting such property.

core_concepts.title: Drafting a Will (Testamentary Disposition)
core_concepts.description:
A Will is the legal declaration of the intention of a testator with respect to their property which they desire to be carried into effect after their death.
- Key Elements: Unlike deeds, a Will takes effect *only after death* and is entirely revocable during the testator's lifetime. 
- Execution (Sec 63, Indian Succession Act): It MUST be attested by at least **two witnesses**, each of whom must have seen the testator sign or affix their mark.

core_concepts.title: Power of Attorney (PoA)
core_concepts.description:
An instrument empowering a specified person to act for and in the name of the person executing it.
- General PoA: Gives the agent broad powers to manage the principal's affairs, properties, and legal matters generally.
- Special PoA: Gives the agent authority to conduct only one specific, isolated act (e.g., executing a single sale deed for a specific property in Delhi).
- Note: The Supreme Court (*Suraj Lamp Case*) has explicitly ruled that a PoA cannot be used as a substitute for a registered Sale Deed to transfer property titles.

important_entities.name: Recitals in a Deed
important_entities.significance: Recitals narrate the background (e.g., 'Whereas the Vendor purchased the land in 2010...'). While they do not transfer property themselves, if the operative part of the deed (Testatum) is ambiguous or unclear, courts will use the Recitals to interpret the true intention of the parties.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Advanced exams ask: 'Is it mandatory to register a Will under Section 17 of the Registration Act if it transfers property worth Rs 50 Crores?' **NO**. Registration of a Will is strictly **optional**, regardless of the property's value. A properly attested unregistered Will is 100% legally valid.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Pre-trial = Liberal; Post-trial = Strict Due Diligence
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember that the stage of the trial determines how generous the judge will be with Order VI Rule 17.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Mains or Judiciary exams, when discussing the transfer of property, explicitly state that drafting a Sale Deed is incomplete without satisfying **Section 17 of the Registration Act** and the **Indian Stamp Act, 1899**, or the document will be barred as evidence under Section 49.
